newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot domestic natgas softens on holiday.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot domestic natgas softens on holiday.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices turned softer Monday in Alberta as demand weakened due to the Heritage Day holiday, traders said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage in Alberta was talked about five cents lower at C$1.43 per gigajoule early and C$1.40 late.
Temperature highs in Calgary climbed into the mid-80s F, according to Weather Services Corp.
"NOVA's packed up, and storage is pretty high," one Calgary-based trader said, noting the excess supply put downward pressure on the market.
At Sumas, Wash., prices were notionally steady at $0.96-1.01 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), though trading was sparse due to the holiday.
The arrival of some heat in the Northwest may trigger additional buying in Tuesday's market as traders return after the holiday.
At Niagara, prices were also notionally flat at $2.34-2.35 per mmBtu despite the rally of NYMEX's September gas futures to a high of $2.385, gaining 14.6 cents from Friday.
